key_insight: On Moscow Exchange equities, quantum-specific features offered no out-of-sample return-ranking advantage over classical controls, while matrix-form QCML behaved like a classical smoothing kernel.
engineering_relevance: Benchmark quantum-inspired financial models against capacity-matched classical controls and normalize feature magnitudes before attributing gains to quantum structure.
method: Progressively removed complex phases and noncommutativity through capacity-matched operator swaps.
Audited spectral crisis indicators against radial-norm nulls and untrained random matrices.
Compared variational circuits and classical controls under trading costs and short-selling bans.
evidence_signal: Using Moscow Exchange daily equities from 2020–2025 with causally lagged macro news, out-of-sample tests found no advantage from phases, noncommutativity, or entanglement; magnitude normalization pushed spectral-gap crisis detection below chance.
watch_item: Results are specific to this noisy equity setting, and reported economic performance did not pass multiple-testing thresholds.
paper_title: Empirical De-Quantization and Norm-Controlled Spectral Audit of Quantum Cognition Machine Learning in an Emerging Equity Market
